description: A slingshot toy: pull the ball back in its elastic socket, let go, and it flies on an arc, bounces off the stage's own edges and settles back into the socket.
interactionNotes: Press the ball and pull it away from the socket: the socket stretches into a capsule that hugs both circles, the arrow inside the ball turns to the direction the throw will take, and the ball trembles once the band is nearly taut. Release and the ball leaves straight back the other way, bounces off the stage's sides and top, loses height, rolls to a stop and fades back into the socket. The further the pull, the faster the throw, and it grows faster than the pull. `power` scales that speed and `bounce` sets how lively every contact is. With the ball focused, the arrow keys aim, Space or Enter throws and Escape puts it back. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the ball does not tremble and the throw leaves no dust.

props.power: Scales the throw, in percent. 100 is the tuned speed; below it the ball is lobbed, above it the ball is fired.
props.bounce: How much speed a contact keeps, 0 to 100. 0 drops the ball dead, 100 keeps almost all of it.
props.socketColor: Color of the socket and of the band once it is stretched. Follows the theme unless set.
props.ballColor: Ball, and the dust the throw leaves behind. Follows the theme unless set.
props.markColor: Color of the arrow inside the ball. Follows the theme unless set.
props.ariaLabel: Accessible name of the ball, for when the default Persian label does not fit the page.
props.autoPreview: Site preview only: it plays the interaction on its own. Leave it off in normal use.

tips: `power` is read at the moment of release, so changing it while the ball sits in the socket changes the next throw; `bounce` is read every frame and can be changed mid-flight.
The toy is a fixed 360 by 260 stage and the physics is measured in those pixels, so give it a box at least that wide instead of shrinking it.
The ball is a real focus target: arrow keys aim, Space or Enter throws, Escape puts the ball back. Keep `ariaLabel` short and in the page's language.
Dust is drawn in `ballColor` and the band in `socketColor`, so both stay in tune when you flip the palette.
Nothing is drawn outside the stage: the ball bounces off the stage edges, so a smaller one needs a softer throw to be playable.
